title: Normalization vanishes at the origin
statement: Let $f : (\bbz/k\bbz)^n \to \bbz/k\bbz$ be any function on the $n$-dimensional space over $\bbz/k\bbz$, and let its normalization be $(\mathrm{normalize}\,f)(x) = f(x) - f(0)$. Then this normalization vanishes at the origin: $(\mathrm{normalize}\,f)(0) = 0$.
hypotheses_covered: f is an arbitrary function from (Z/kZ)^n to Z/kZ
k is a positive modulus (NeZero k)
